speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and have you had any recent trauma or injuries to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Can you tell me if the finger is bent at an unusual angle, and are you able to fully straighten or bend it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms—specifically the inability to flex the fingertip and the finger resting in extension—strongly suggest a Jersey Finger injury, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. To confirm this before proceeding, do you feel any clicking sensation when you attempt to move the finger, and is there a palpable gap or defect at the base of the fingertip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of a forced pull on the flexed finger during football, combined with the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger resting in extension, is classic for a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion. I will request imaging to confirm the diagnosis and assess for any associated bony avulsion. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand
